mainTopic: שלמה's marriage to פרעה's daughter, and which converts from עמון, מואב, מצרים and אדום may marry into the קהל
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion about שלמה marrying פרעה's daughter. She was a first-generation מצרית, and a ברייתא about מנימין the Egyptian convert shows that this ban still applied. רב פפא answers that שלמה never truly married his foreign wives. The פסוק says ״ויתחתן״ only because he loved her so much. Next, רב אשי shows רבינא that the משנה about a פצוע דכא can't prove anything about a נתינה, because its beginning and end imply opposite things. A new משנה then teaches that male עמוני and מואבי converts are banned forever, but their women are permitted right away. מצרי and אדומי converts are banned for three generations, and רבי שמעון permits their women immediately as a received הלכה. The גמרא finds the source in the story of שאול asking about דוד's lineage. There אבנר answers דואג with עמוני ולא עמונית, and the בית המדרש confirms this הלכה. The answer to דואג's last question comes on the next amud.

steps.title: פרעה's daughter had no need to convert for gain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its earlier point: the worry that converts in שלמה's time joined only for royal benefits does not apply to פרעה's daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this one did not need such things.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes off an earlier discussion. It says פרעה's daughter was already royalty, so nobody would suspect she converted just to gain the good life of שלמה's kingdom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא said converts were not accepted in the days of דוד and שלמה, because people might be converting for personal gain. Here it answers that this suspicion does not fit a princess who already had everything. So that concern does not explain why her marriage would be a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: She did not need it (she had no need for the benefits)

phrases.english: But this one did not need such things.
phrases.notes: "This one" is פרעה's daughter. She was already a princess, so she had no reason to convert just to get royal benefits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the earlier discussion from before this section about suspected converts in שלמה's time.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the reason for suspicion does not apply to her
steps.terutzHavaAmina: פרעה's daughter should be suspect like other converts in שלמה's time.
steps.terutzMaskana: As a princess she had no motive of gain, so that suspicion does not apply.

steps.title: She was a first-generation Egyptian anyway
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we need any other reason. She was a first-generation מצרית convert, who is forbidden to marry into the קהל.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him derive it from the fact that she was a first-generation Egyptian convert!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a challenge. Even if she converted sincerely, the Torah forbids a first-generation Egyptian convert from marrying a born Jew.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah says Egyptian converts may enter the קהל only from the third generation. פרעה's daughter was clearly first generation. So the marriage should have been forbidden for this simple reason, no matter how sincere she was.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him derive it instead (why not use this simpler reason?)

phrases.english: But let him derive it from the fact that she is a first-generation Egyptian!
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are the corrected wording. The rule about Egyptians is in דברים 23:8–9.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתִיפּוֹק לֵיהּ דְּהָא מִצְרִית רִאשׁוֹנָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After solving the suspicion problem, the גמרא raises a different and stronger problem.
steps.kashyaTarget: The validity of שלמה's marriage to פרעה's daughter
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Torah forbids first-generation Egyptian converts from marrying into the קהל, and she was one.

steps.title: A suggested escape: today's Egyptians are different people
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests an answer: maybe the Egyptians the Torah forbade have scattered, and those living in Egypt now are other nations.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: those original Egyptians went off into the world, and these are other people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer to the challenge, but only so it can knock it down next. This line sets up the following proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that the nations got mixed up, so the people living in Egypt are not the Egyptians the Torah meant. If so, פרעה's daughter would not count as a true מצרית. The phrase וכי תימא tells us the גמרא is not going to accept this.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (introduces a suggestion that will be rejected)
They went off into the world (they scattered)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the גמרא's real answer. וכי תימא offers an idea only so the next line can reject it.

phrases.english: And if you would say: those went off into the world,
phrases.notes: "Those" are the original Egyptians the Torah forbade.

phrases.english: and these are other people,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes a possible defense against the challenge in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the category: the Egyptians in Egypt now are not the ones the Torah meant
steps.terutzHavaAmina: פרעה's daughter was a first-generation Egyptian and forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: Maybe she was not a true Egyptian at all, because the nations got mixed up.

steps.title: מנימין the Egyptian convert shows the ban still applied
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that even in the days of רבי עקיבא's students, Egyptian converts still kept the generation rule. So the escape fails.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is taught in a ברייתא: רבי יהודה said, מנימין, an Egyptian convert, was a friend of mine from the students of רבי עקיבא. He said: I am a first-generation Egyptian, and I married a first-generation Egyptian. I will marry my son to a second-generation Egyptian, so that my grandson will be fit to enter the קהל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion from step 3. It quotes a ברייתא showing that Egyptian converts were still treated as Egyptians long after שלמה's time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מנימין carefully planned his family's marriages so his grandson would be third generation and allowed to marry into the קהל. This only makes sense if the Torah's Egyptian rule still applied to Egyptians of his day. If it applied then, it surely applied to פרעה's daughter, so the challenge from step 2 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is taught in a ברייתא (introduces a source against the suggestion)
To enter the congregation (to marry a born Jew)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the rabbis treated the Egyptian generation rule as still in force in their own time.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: Rabbi Yehuda said:

phrases.aramaic: מִנְיָמִין גֵּר מִצְרִי הָיָה לִי חָבֵר
phrases.english: Minyamin, an Egyptian convert, was a friend of mine
from among the students of Rabbi Akiva,
he said: I am a first-generation Egyptian,
and I married a first-generation Egyptian woman.
I will marry my son to a second-generation Egyptian woman
so that my grandson will be
fit to enter the congregation!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Knocks down the escape offered in step 3 and brings back the challenge from step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that today's Egyptians are not the Egyptians the Torah forbade
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא shows the Egyptian generation rule was still kept in the time of רבי עקיבא's students.

steps.title: רב פפא: שלמה never truly married any of them
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says we cannot prove anything from שלמה, because his marriages to foreign women were never real marriages.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Shall we stand up and object from שלמה? שלמה did not marry anyone, as it is written about him: "Of the nations concerning which ה׳ said to the children of Israel, You shall not go among them, neither shall they come among you; for surely they will turn away your heart after their gods; שלמה cleaved to these in love."
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the challenge. He says שלמה's foreign wives were never legally married to him, so his case teaches us nothing about the law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says שלמה "cleaved to them in love," not that he married them. So all of his foreign marriages, including פרעה's daughter, were not valid. That means there is no special question about her being a first-generation Egyptian.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we stand up and object?
He did not marry anyone at all
Cleaved in love (attached himself, without a real marriage)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Shall we stand up and raise an objection from Solomon?
Solomon did not marry anyone,
as it is written about him:

phrases.aramaic: ״מִן הַגּוֹיִם אֲשֶׁר אָמַר ה׳ אֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: "Of the nations concerning which the Lord said to the children of Israel,
phrases.notes: מלכים א 11:2

phrases.aramaic: לֹא תָבוֹאוּ בָּהֶם וְהֵם לֹא יָבוֹאוּ בָכֶם
phrases.english: You shall not go among them, neither shall they come among you;

phrases.aramaic: אָכֵן יַטּוּ אֶת לְבַבְכֶם אַחֲרֵי אֱלֹהֵיהֶם,
phrases.english: for surely they will turn away your heart after their gods;
Solomon cleaved to these in love."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא אֲנַן מִשְּׁלֹמֹה לֵיקוּ וְנֹתֵיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the escape in step 3 failed, רב פפא answers the challenge from step 2 in a new way.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejecting the starting point: there was never a valid marriage to question
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שלמה validly married פרעה's daughter, which seems to break the Egyptian rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: None of שלמה's foreign marriages were valid. He was only attached to them, so there is no proof from him.

steps.title: The word "and he married" remains difficult
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits one problem is left. The פסוק about פרעה's daughter says ״ויתחתן״, "and he married," which sounds like a real marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the word "and he married" is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רב פפא's answer does not seem to fit. For פרעה's daughter the פסוק uses a word that sounds like a real marriage. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא said שלמה only "cleaved" to his foreign wives. But for פרעה's daughter, the פסוק says ״ויתחתן״, which sounds like he truly married into פרעה's family. This wording seems to stand against רב פפא's answer until the גמרא explains it in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is still difficult (a problem that remains)
And he married / became related by marriage

steps.whatToRemember: פרעה's daughter was a first-generation Egyptian, and the ברייתא of מנימין shows that rule still applied. רב פפא answers that שלמה's foreign marriages were never valid. The word ״ויתחתן״ seems to challenge that answer, and the next step resolves it.

phrases.english: But "and he married" is difficult!
phrases.notes: מלכים א 3:1, where the פסוק says שלמה married into פרעה's family.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points out a remaining problem with רב פפא's answer in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim that שלמה never truly married his foreign wives
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק uses ״ויתחתן״ for פרעה's daughter, which means a real marriage.

steps.title: His great love made the verse call it a marriage
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק calls it ״ויתחתן״ only because שלמה loved פרעה's daughter so much, not because it was a valid marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he loved her so much, the פסוק treats him as if he had married her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the leftover problem from step 6. The word ״ויתחתן״ does not show a real marriage. It shows how strongly שלמה loved her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 6 the word ״ויתחתן״ seemed to prove the marriage was real, which would undo רב פפא's answer. Now the גמרא says the פסוק is describing his feelings, not the legal status. So רב פפא's answer still stands: the marriage was never legally valid.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק treats him as if

steps.whatToRemember: שלמה's marriages to foreign women were not valid marriages. The פסוק says ״ויתחתן״ only to show how much he loved פרעה's daughter.

phrases.english: Because of the extra love that he loved her,
the verse treats him
as if he had married her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 6 and saves רב פפא's answer from step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the wording of the פסוק as describing feelings, not legal status.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״ויתחתן״ means a real, legally valid marriage.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״ויתחתן״ describes his great love. Legally there was no marriage.

steps.title: רבינא's challenge: the משנה implies a פצוע דכא may not marry a נתינה
steps.stepSummary: רבינא points out that the משנה lists only a convert and a freed maidservant as permitted, which suggests a נתינה is forbidden to a פצוע דכא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: But we learned in a משנה that a פצוע דכא and a כרות שפכה may marry a convert and a freed maidservant. That implies they may not marry a נתינה!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא challenges the teaching that a פצוע דכא may marry a נתינה. He reads an implication into a משנה that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה names only two kinds of women a פצוע דכא may marry: a convert and a freed maidservant. רבינא argues that if a נתינה were also allowed, the משנה would have said so. So its silence suggests a נתינה is forbidden to him.

keyTerms.meaning: A man with crushed testicles, who may not marry a woman born Jewish
A man whose organ has been cut off
A woman descended from the גבעונים

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה never openly says "a נתינה is forbidden." רבינא is reading an implication from what it leaves out ("הָא..."). That kind of reading is exactly what רב אשי will question next.

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi,
But didn't we learn in a mishna:
A man with crushed testicles and one whose organ is cut off
are permitted to a female convert and a freed maidservant.
This implies that with a Gibeonite woman they are forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from the שלמה discussion to challenge the ruling that a פצוע דכא may marry a נתינה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The teaching that a פצוע דכא is permitted to marry a נתינה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה lists only a convert and a freed maidservant as permitted. That implies a נתינה is forbidden.

steps.title: רב אשי: the end of the same משנה implies the opposite
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי shows that the משנה's next line implies a נתינה is permitted, so no conclusion can be drawn from either implication.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי answered: By your logic, read the end of the משנה: "They are forbidden only from entering the קהל." That implies a נתינה is permitted! So nothing can be learned from this משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי rejects רבינא's challenge. The same kind of reading, used on the end of the משנה, gives the opposite result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part of the משנה seems to forbid a נתינה. The last part says they are forbidden only from the קהל, and a נתינה is not part of the קהל, so it seems to permit her. Since the two implications cancel each other out, the משנה proves nothing, and the original ruling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of a משנה or ברייתא
To enter the congregation, meaning to marry a woman born Jewish
Nothing can be learned from it

steps.whatToRemember: When the beginning and the end of a משנה imply opposite things, the גמרא does not use either implication as a proof. Here, the ruling that a פצוע דכא may marry a נתינה stays in place.

phrases.english: He said to him: And according to your reasoning,
say the latter clause:
And they are forbidden only from entering the congregation.
This implies that with a Gibeonite woman they are permitted!
Rather, nothing can be learned from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבינא's implication by showing a contradictory implication in the same משנה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof drawn from the משנה's wording. It does not prove the opposite from the משנה either.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The implication from the first part is cancelled by an opposite implication from the last part.

steps.title: New משנה: male עמוני and מואבי converts are forbidden forever, but their women are permitted right away
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that male עמוני and מואבי converts may never marry into the קהל, while female converts from these nations are permitted immediately.
steps.simpleTranslation: עמוני and מואבי converts are forbidden, and their prohibition lasts forever. But their women are permitted right away.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic: converts from עמון and מואב. It gives the basic rule for men and for women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the מצרי rule, where the ban ends after a few generations, the ban on male עמוני and מואבי converts never ends. Women from these nations are not included at all, so even a first-generation female convert may marry into the קהל.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מתניתין, "our משנה"; marks the start of a new משנה
Converts from the nations of עמון and מואב
A permanent prohibition, for all generations
Their women, the female converts of these nations

steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה is the basis for the permitted marriage of a מואבית convert like רות.

phrases.english: MISHNA: An Ammonite and a Moabite are forbidden,
phrases.notes: Forbidden to marry a woman born Jewish ("to enter the קהל").

phrases.english: and their prohibition is an eternal prohibition.
But their women are permitted immediately.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה and a new topic after the previous discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Male עמוני and מואבי converts are forbidden to marry into the קהל forever. Their female converts are permitted immediately.

steps.title: Egyptian and Edomite converts are forbidden for three generations
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that מצרי and אדומי converts may not marry into the קהל for three generations. This applies to both men and women.
steps.simpleTranslation: An Egyptian or Edomite convert is forbidden only for three generations, men and women alike.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves from עמון and מואב to a second group, converts from מצרים and אדום. Their ban is limited to three generations and covers both men and women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With עמון and מואב, the men were banned forever and the women were permitted right away. Here the ban is shorter, only three generations, but it covers women as well as men. This contrast sets up רבי שמעון's argument in the next step.

phrases.english: An Egyptian and an Edomite
are not forbidden
except for three generations,
both males and females.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִצְרִי וַאֲדוֹמִי אֵינָם אֲסוּרִים אֶלָּא עַד שְׁלֹשָׁה דּוֹרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה from step 10, moving from עמון and מואב to מצרים and אדום.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מצרי and אדומי converts, both men and women, are forbidden to marry into the קהל for three generations.

steps.title: רבי שמעון permits the women right away
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון disagrees with the first opinion. He says Egyptian and Edomite women are permitted immediately.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון permits the women immediately.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון gives a different ruling. He agrees about the men but says the women are permitted right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion treated men and women the same. רבי שמעון splits them, just as the משנה split them for עמון and מואב.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon permits
the females immediately.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַתִּיר אֶת הַנְּקֵבוֹת מִיָּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the ruling of step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Female Egyptian and Edomite converts may marry into the קהל immediately.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's logical argument from עמון and מואב
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון supports his view with a קל וחומר. Where the men are banned forever (עמון and מואב), the women are permitted right away. So where the men are banned for only three generations, the women should surely be permitted right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said: This follows from a קל וחומר. If the תורה permitted the women immediately where it banned the men forever, then surely where it banned the men for only three generations, we should permit the women immediately.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון proves his opinion with a logical argument. It moves from the stricter case to the more lenient one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עמון and מואב are the stricter case, since the men are banned forever, yet even there the women are permitted. מצרים and אדום are the more lenient case, so the women there should be permitted too. That is the basic shape of a קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a stricter case to a more lenient one, or the reverse

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said:
The matter follows from a kal vachomer:
If in a place
where it forbade the males with a permanent ban
phrases.notes: This is עמון and מואב, from the previous part of the משנה.

phrases.english: it permitted the females immediately,
then a place where it forbade the males
only for three generations

phrases.aramaic: — אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁנַּתִּיר אֶת הַנְּקֵבוֹת מִיָּד?
phrases.english: is it not logical that we should permit the females immediately?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, קַל וָחוֹמֶר הַדְּבָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind רבי שמעון's ruling in step 12.
steps.raayaObject: רבי שמעון's ruling that Egyptian and Edomite women are permitted immediately.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from the law of עמון and מואב.

steps.title: The חכמים: a tradition we accept, logic we can answer
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים tell רבי שמעון that if he received this as a הלכה, they will accept it. If he is relying on his own logic, they have a rebuttal.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: If this is a received הלכה, we will accept it. But if it is based on logic, there is a rebuttal.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back on רבי שמעון's קל וחומר. They say logic alone can be refuted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים do not attack a tradition. They attack only the logic, saying the קל וחומר has a flaw. The משנה does not tell us what their rebuttal is.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, a law received by tradition from one's teachers

phrases.english: They said to him:
If it is a received halacha, we will accept it;
but if it is from logic, there is a rebuttal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אִם הֲלָכָה — נְקַבֵּל, וְאִם לַדִּין — יֵשׁ תְּשׁוּבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the קל וחומר of step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the logical proof, not a possible tradition.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The חכמים claim the קל וחומר can be refuted, though they do not say how.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: I am stating a tradition
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says his ruling is a הלכה he received, not just his own logic.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Not so. I am stating a הלכה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון answers the חכמים. His ruling is based on a tradition, so their rebuttal of the logic does not undo it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the words לא כי, רבי שמעון also rejects the idea that his קל וחומר can be refuted. Either way, by saying it is a הלכה he takes the ruling out of the realm of debate. The חכמים had already said they would accept a tradition.

phrases.english: He said to them: Not so;
I am stating a received halacha.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם: לֹא כִּי, הֲלָכָה אֲנִי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the חכמים' pushback in step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ruling is a tradition from his teachers, so a rebuttal of the logic does not cancel it.
steps.whatToRemember: מצרי and אדומי converts are forbidden for three generations. רבי שמעון permits their women right away, and he says this is a received הלכה.

steps.title: What is the source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its discussion by asking for the source of the משנה's ruling that female עמוני and מואבי converts are permitted immediately.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where are these matters derived?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking where the משנה gets its rule. It is setting up the next step, where a source will be brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question goes back to the ruling about עמון and מואב (step 10), that only the men are banned. The גמרא wants a source showing that the women are permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these matters derived?

phrases.english: Gemara: From where are these matters derived?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is asking about step 10: how do we know female עמוני and מואבי converts are permitted right away?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that female עמוני and מואבי converts are permitted immediately.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן brings שאול's question about דוד
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן quotes the פסוק where שאול sees דוד going out to fight גלית and asks אבנר whose son the youth is. אבנר says he does not know.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: As the verse says, "When שאול saw דוד going out toward the Philistine, he said to אבנר, the commander of the army: Whose son is this youth, אבנר? And אבנר said: By your life, O king, I do not know."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן starts to answer the question by quoting a פסוק about שאול, דוד, and אבנר. The גמרא will first work out what שאול was really asking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far this is only the פסוק. It is not yet clear how it relates to our law. The next steps will show that the question was about דוד's family line, which goes back to רות the מואביה.

keyTerms.meaning: אבנר, the commander of the army

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: As the verse states:
"And when Saul saw David
phrases.notes: שמואל א 17:55

phrases.english: going out toward the Philistine,
he said to Abner, the commander of the army:
Whose son is this youth, Abner?
And Abner said:
As your soul lives, O king, I do not know."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source starts from שאול's question about דוד's lineage. The full explanation comes later.

steps.title: But שאול knew דוד well
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how שאול could fail to know דוד. An earlier פסוק says שאול loved him greatly and made him his armor-bearer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Didn't he know him? But it is written: "And he loved him greatly, and he became his armor-bearer."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the simple reading of the פסוק. שאול already knew דוד personally.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If דוד was שאול's own armor-bearer, שאול could not have been asking who דוד was. So the question "whose son" must mean something else.

phrases.english: And did he not know him?
But isn't it written:
"And he loved him greatly,
phrases.notes: שמואל א 16:21

phrases.english: and he became his armor-bearer"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the plain meaning of the פסוק quoted in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The plain reading that שאול did not know who דוד was.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another פסוק shows that שאול knew and loved דוד as his armor-bearer.

steps.title: He was asking about דוד's father
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that שאול was asking about דוד's father, not about דוד himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he was asking about his father.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reinterprets the question "whose son is this?" as a question about דוד's father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שאול knew דוד, so the words "whose son" must be about his father and family background. This keeps the two פסוקים from contradicting each other.

keyTerms.meaning: He was asking about his father

phrases.english: Rather, he was asking about his father.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שאול was asking who דוד himself was.
steps.terutzMaskana: שאול was asking about דוד's father.

steps.title: But everyone knew ישי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how שאול could fail to know ישי. A פסוק describes him as an important man, and רב (or רבי אבא) explains that he came and went with crowds.
steps.simpleTranslation: And didn't he know his father? But it is written: "And the man was old in the days of שאול, coming among men," and רב (some say רבי אבא) said: This is ישי, דוד's father, who went in with a crowd and came out with a crowd!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges its own answer. ישי was famous, so how could שאול not know who he was?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being surrounded by crowds shows that ישי was a well-known, important figure. So שאול's question cannot simply mean "who is his father?" The גמרא will need yet another explanation of what שאול was asking.

phrases.english: And did he not know his father?
But isn't it written:
"And the man, in the days of Saul,
phrases.notes: שמואל א 17:12

phrases.english: was old, coming among men,"
and Rav said, and some say Rabbi Abba:
This is Jesse, the father of David,
who went in with a crowd
and came out with a crowd!
phrases.notes: He means ישי was such an important man that people always surrounded him, so everyone knew him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that שאול was asking about דוד's father.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ישי was a famous man surrounded by crowds, so שאול must have known him.

steps.title: שאול was asking whether דוד came from פרץ or זרח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that שאול's question was really about which branch of יהודה דוד's family came from: פרץ, the royal line, or זרח, the line of important people.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what שאול meant: Is he from פרץ or from זרח? If from פרץ, he will be king, because a king breaks through a path and nobody can stop him. If from זרח, he will just be an important person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 20 (how could שאול not know ישי?). It explains that שאול knew ישי, but wanted to know which family line he came from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שאול was not asking for ישי's name. He was asking about ancestry: פרץ means royalty, and זרח means only importance. The link to kingship comes from a wordplay: פרץ sounds like פורץ, 'breaks through', which is what a king may do.

keyTerms.meaning: Son of יהודה; the line that kings come from
Son of יהודה; a line of important but non-royal people
Breaks through to make a path (a king's right)

phrases.english: This is what Saul was saying:

phrases.aramaic: אִי מִפֶּרֶץ אָתֵי, אִי מִזֶּרַח אָתֵי?
phrases.english: Does he come from Peretz, or does he come from Zerach?
If he comes from Peretz, he will be king,
for a king breaks through to make a path for himself
phrases.notes: There's a play on words here: פורץ ('breaks through') sounds like פרץ.

phrases.english: and no one can stop him.

phrases.aramaic: אִי מִזֶּרַח אָתֵי — חֲשִׁיבָא בְּעָלְמָא הָוֵי.
phrases.english: If he comes from Zerach, he will merely be an important man.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 20 by changing what שאול's question was about.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the question in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שאול did not know who ישי was.
steps.terutzMaskana: שאול knew ישי, but was asking about his ancestry: פרץ or זרח.

steps.title: Why did שאול tell אבנר to inquire about דוד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why שאול suddenly cared about דוד's ancestry.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why did שאול tell אבנר, 'Go ask about him'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what made שאול want to look into דוד's family. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 explained what שאול asked. Now the גמרא wants to know why he asked at that moment.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא אֲמַר לֵיהּ שַׁאֵל עֲלֵיהּ,
phrases.english: For what reason did he say to him, 'Inquire about him'?
phrases.notes: שאול is talking to אבנר. The words 'go ask' come from שמואל א 17:56, which the גמרא quotes in step 32.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא אֲמַר לֵיהּ שַׁאֵל עֲלֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on step 21 by asking what caused שאול's concern.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What made שאול worry about דוד's ancestry.

steps.title: שאול's clothes fit דוד
steps.stepSummary: שאול dressed דוד in his own clothes and they fit, even though שאול was taller than everyone. This made שאול suspect that דוד was destined to be king.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it says 'שאול dressed דוד in his clothes (מדיו)', which means they were his size. And about שאול it says, 'From his shoulders and up he was taller than all the people.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the clothes fit דוד. That was a sign to שאול that דוד might be the next king.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מדיו is read as כמדתו, 'his size'. שאול was unusually tall, so if his clothes fit דוד, דוד matched the king. That is why שאול wanted to check whether דוד came from the royal line of פרץ.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'And Saul clad David with his garments,'
phrases.notes: שמואל א 17:38

phrases.english: meaning: of his size.
And it is written about Saul:
'From his shoulders and upward he was taller than all the people.'
phrases.notes: שמואל א 9:2

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב וַיַּלְבֵּשׁ שָׁאוּל אֶת דָּוִד מַדָּיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שאול's clothes fit דוד, which hinted that דוד was fit for kingship.

steps.title: דואג questions whether דוד may even marry into the Jewish people
steps.stepSummary: דואג האדומי says that before asking whether דוד is fit to be king, שאול should ask whether he may enter the קהל at all, since he descends from רות המואביה.
steps.simpleTranslation: דואג האדומי said to him: Before you ask whether he is fit for kingship, ask whether he is allowed to enter the קהל. Why? Because he comes from רות the Moabite.
steps.whatsHappening: דואג raises a serious challenge to דוד's lineage. He says that because דוד comes from a Moabite woman, he might be barred from marrying a Jew.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה says a מואבי may never enter the קהל. דואג assumes this includes women too, so רות's descendants would be disqualified. This is the exact question behind the משנה's rule that female Moabites are permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Doeg the Edomite, an advisor of שאול
To enter the congregation, meaning to marry a born Jew

phrases.english: Doeg the Edomite said to him:
Before you inquire about him

phrases.aramaic: אִם הָגוּן הוּא לַמַּלְכוּת אִם לָאו,
phrases.english: whether or not he is fit for kingship,

phrases.aramaic: שְׁאַל עָלָיו אִם רָאוּי לָבֹא בַּקָּהָל אִם לָאו.
phrases.english: inquire whether or not he is fit to enter the congregation.
What is the reason? Because he comes from Ruth the Moabite.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves the discussion from kingship to whether דוד's lineage is valid at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: דוד's fitness to enter the קהל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ban on מואבי seems to cover women too, so the descendants of רות would be barred.

steps.title: אבנר: the ban is on מואבי men, not women
steps.stepSummary: אבנר answers that the ban applies only to male עמוני and מואבי, not to females.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבנר said to him: We learned, 'an עמוני' and not an עמונית; 'a מואבי' and not a מואבית.
steps.whatsHappening: אבנר defends דוד. The תורה wrote the male form, so women like רות are permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the source the גמרא was looking for in step 16. The masculine words עמוני and מואבי in the פסוק limit the ban to men, so רות was allowed to marry into the Jewish people.

keyTerms.meaning: An Ammonite man, not an Ammonite woman
A Moabite man, not a Moabite woman

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the משנה's ruling that female עמוני and מואבי converts are permitted right away.

phrases.english: Abner said to him: We have learned:
'An Ammonite,' but not an Ammonite woman.
'A Moabite,' but not a Moabite woman.
phrases.notes: From the פסוק in דברים 23:4.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers דואג's challenge from step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise reading of the פסוק's wording (male form)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ban on מואבי includes women.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only male עמוני and מואבי are banned.

steps.title: Then would a ממזרת also be permitted?
steps.stepSummary: דואג challenges: if the male form excludes women, then ממזר should exclude a female ממזרת too, which is not true.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then 'a ממזר' should mean only a male, and not a ממזרת?
steps.whatsHappening: דואג attacks אבנר's reading. Using the same logic, a female ממזר would be permitted, and everyone knows she is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about ממזר is also written in the male form. If the male form always limits a law to men, a ממזרת could marry into the קהל. Since that is wrong, אבנר's method seems broken.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so (pushes an idea to an unacceptable result)
A child born from a forbidden relationship

phrases.english: But if that is so:
'A mamzer,' but not a female mamzer?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading method used in step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: אבנר's rule that the male form excludes women
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same logic would wrongly permit a ממזרת.

steps.title: ממזר means 'a strange blemish'
steps.stepSummary: אבנר answers that the word ממזר is read as מום זר, 'a strange blemish', which describes the person regardless of gender.
steps.simpleTranslation: It says ממזר, which means מום זר, a strange blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: אבנר explains why ממזר is different. The word describes a defect, not just a male person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מום זר describes a flaw that comes from a forbidden relationship. That flaw exists in a woman just as much as in a man, so the male form of the word does not limit it.

phrases.english: It is written 'mamzer', meaning: a strange blemish.
phrases.notes: He's splitting the word ממזר into מום זר, so it describes a flaw, not a male person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 26.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ממזר is a male noun, like מואבי.
steps.terutzMaskana: ממזר describes a defect that applies to both men and women.

steps.title: Then would an Egyptian woman also be permitted?
steps.stepSummary: דואג challenges again: the פסוק about מצרי is also in the male form, so the same logic would permit an Egyptian woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then 'a מצרי' and not a מצרית!
steps.whatsHappening: דואג brings another case. If male wording limits the law, Egyptian women would be permitted, which is not the case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ממזר answer only worked because of that word's special meaning. מצרי has no such special meaning, so דואג says אבנר's method still fails.

keyTerms.meaning: An Egyptian convert, banned for three generations

phrases.english: Then 'an Egyptian,' but not an Egyptian woman!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to אבנר's reading after the ממזר challenge was answered.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same logic would permit an Egyptian woman, which is wrong.

steps.title: The Torah gives a reason that fits only men
steps.stepSummary: אבנר answers that עמון and מואב are different because the תורה gives the reason: they did not greet the Jews with bread and water. That is something men do, not women.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it is different, because the reason of the פסוק is written: 'Because they did not greet you with bread and water.' It is a man's way to go out and greet, not a woman's way.
steps.whatsHappening: אבנר explains why עמון and מואב are not like מצרים. The תורה's stated reason for the ban only fits men.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban comes as a punishment for not greeting the Jews. Since only men normally went out to greet, only the men are guilty, so only the men are banned. The ban on מצרי has no such reason, so it covers women too.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason given by the פסוק

phrases.english: Here it is different, because the reason of the verse is stated explicitly:
'Because they did not meet you
with bread and with water' —
phrases.notes: דברים 23:5

phrases.english: it is the way of a man to go out and greet,
and it is not the way of a woman to go out and greet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the מצרי challenge of step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction based on the stated reason of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ban on מואבי works like the ban on מצרי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The reason for the ban on עמון and מואב applies only to men, so only men are banned.

steps.title: The women should have greeted the women
steps.stepSummary: דואג objects: even if women don't greet men, the Moabite women should have gone out to greet the Jewish women.
steps.simpleTranslation: They should have greeted: men going out to greet men, and women going out to greet women!
steps.whatsHappening: דואג attacks the reason אבנר just gave. Women could have greeted women, so the Moabite women are also guilty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבנר's answer depended on women having no duty to greet. דואג says the duty could have been met in a modest way, women greeting women. If so, the women share the guilt and should share the ban.

phrases.english: They should have gone out to greet:
men to meet the men
and women to meet the women!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיָה לָהֶם לְקַדֵּם אֲנָשִׁים לִקְרַאת אֲנָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that women had no duty to greet
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Women could have greeted women, so Moabite women are also guilty.

steps.title: אבנר falls silent
steps.stepSummary: אבנר has no answer to דואג's last question and stays silent.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was silent.
steps.whatsHappening: אבנר cannot answer, so the question stays open for now. This sets up the next part of the story, where an answer will be needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבנר's silence does not mean the rule is wrong. It only means he could not answer this question, so דוד's status is still being challenged.
steps.confusionAlert: אבנר's silence does not overturn the הלכה. The rule that a מואבית is permitted still stands; only the answer to דואג's question is missing here.

phrases.english: He was silent.
phrases.notes: It's אבנר who goes quiet, since he couldn't answer דואג.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the קשיא of step 30 went unanswered by אבנר.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: דואג's question stands unanswered for now, which sets up the continuation of the story.

steps.title: The king says: ask whose son this lad is
steps.stepSummary: Right after אבנר falls silent, the גמרא quotes the פסוק where שאול tells him to inquire whose son the 'עלם' is.
steps.simpleTranslation: Immediately: 'And the king said: You go ask whose son this lad is.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the story by quoting the next פסוק, where שאול speaks right after אבנר could not answer. This sets up the next move, a close look at one word in this פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'מיד' (immediately) ties this פסוק directly to the moment אבנר went silent. The גמרא is about to read the word 'העלם' as more than just 'lad'.

phrases.english: Immediately: "And the king said:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁאַל אַתָּה בֶּן מִי זֶה הָעָלֶם״.
phrases.english: You go ask whose son this lad is."
phrases.notes: שמואל א 17:56. In the פסוק, שאול is speaking to אבנר.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיָּד: וַיֹּאמֶר הַמֶּלֶךְ שְׁאַל אַתָּה בֶּן מִי זֶה הָעָלֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story right after אבנר's silence, bringing the next פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שאול immediately tells him to inquire about the 'עלם'.

steps.title: Why does the פסוק switch from 'נער' to 'עלם'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notices that the earlier פסוק calls דוד a 'נער' while this one calls him an 'עלם', and asks why.
steps.simpleTranslation: There he calls him 'youth' (נער), and here he calls him 'lad' (עלם)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the wording changed between two פסוקים right next to each other. This question sets up the hidden message the גמרא is about to find.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both words mean a young man, so a change in wording suggests the פסוק is hinting at something. The question is not an attack; it is looking for the meaning behind the change.

phrases.english: There he calls him "youth,"
phrases.notes: In the פסוק just before (שמואל א 17:55), שאול asks 'בן מי זה הנער'.

phrases.english: and here he calls him "lad"?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם קָרֵי לֵיהּ נַעַר, הָכָא קָרֵי לֵיהּ עֶלֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes a word in the פסוק just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the פסוק changes from 'נער' to 'עלם'.

steps.title: The hint: the הלכה was hidden from you
steps.stepSummary: The word 'עלם' hints at 'נתעלמה': שאול is saying the הלכה is hidden from you, so go ask in the בית המדרש.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he was telling him: The הלכה is hidden from you. Go and ask in the study hall.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'עלם' is a wordplay on 'נתעלמה' (hidden). שאול was telling him that he doesn't know the הלכה and must go ask in the בית המדרש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since nobody could answer דואג's last question, שאול's words are read as sending the matter to the experts. The change from 'נער' to 'עלם' carries this message.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he was telling him

phrases.english: This is what he was saying to him:
The halakha is hidden from you —
phrases.notes: The word נתעלמה shares its letters with עלם, so 'עלם' is the hint.

phrases.english: go out and ask in the study hall.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָא אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הֲלָכָה נִתְעַלְּמָה מִמְּךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the change in wording.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'עלם' hints at 'נתעלמה': the הלכה is hidden from you, go ask in the בית המדרש.

steps.title: The ruling: a male עמוני or מואבי, not a female
steps.stepSummary: He asks in the בית המדרש, and they rule that only a male עמוני or מואבי is forbidden, not a female.
steps.simpleTranslation: He asked. They told him: 'An Ammonite' — not an Ammonite woman. 'A Moabite' — not a Moabite woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The question is taken to the בית המדרש, and the answer is a clear הלכה: the ban applies to men from עמון and מואב, not women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though אבנר could not answer דואג's last question in his own words, the הלכה itself was known in the בית המדרש. This supports that רות, a woman from מואב, was permitted, so דוד's lineage is valid. The answer to דואג's question about women greeting women comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: A male Ammonite, not a female Ammonite
A male Moabite, not a female Moabite

steps.whatToRemember: The final הלכה from the בית המדרש: 'עמוני ולא עמונית, מואבי ולא מואבית'. Only men from עמון and מואב are forbidden to marry into the Jewish people, so רות and her descendant דוד are fully valid.
steps.confusionAlert: אבנר's silence did not mean the הלכה was in doubt. He just could not explain it himself; the בית המדרש confirmed the הלכה as known.

phrases.english: He asked, and they said to him:
"An Ammonite," but not an Ammonite woman.
"A Moabite," but not a Moabite woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאַל, אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: עַמּוֹנִי וְלֹא עַמּוֹנִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out the instruction to ask in the בית המדרש and records the answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ban on עמון and מואב applies only to males; females are permitted.
